author: Holly E. Newton
title: Halloween Boo Books - Meridian Magazine
text:
Halloween books are always a favorite with young readers, and there are so many wonderful choices for the season. From sturdy board books for the littlest readers to picture books and middle-grade stories, there is something for children of every age. The books below offer a fun mix of silly, sweet, spooky, and slightly scary Halloween stories. The appropriate age range is listed with each book.
The Skeleton and the Cat, by Brandon James Scott, is actually a sweet story about friendship. The Skeleton doesn’t want any visitors. She is perfectly happy being alone, watering her plants and drinking her tea. But when the Cat shows up, he begins to befriend her whether she likes it or not. The story is told in five short chapters, making it a nice choice for young readers who are ready for a longer story. The illustrations are bright, beautiful, and add to the charm of this sweet friendship tale.
House of Harness (A Scarlet Witch Graphic Novel) , by Preeti Chhibber and colorfully illustrated by Jodi Nishijima and Kiichi Mizushima, follows teen Wanda Eger as she begins at a magical school. She quickly finds a nemesis in another student, but the two must put their differences aside and work together to deal with a bad element threatening the school. Filled with magic, adventure, and plenty of action, this graphic novel is a fun choice for readers ages eight through twelve.
Pumpkin Apocalypse , by M. D. Payne, introduces newcomer Adam, who is nervous because he has some big issues with pumpkins. When he is paired with Molly, who is obsessed with pumpkins, the two must work together on the Pumpkin Fest. This middle-grade book is great fun, with just enough spooky excitement throughout to make it a perfect Halloween read. The unlikely partnership between Adam and Molly adds plenty of humor to the story.
Halloween (Water Wonders) , published by Kane Miller and cleverly and brightly illustrated by Laura Garrido Amador, is a colorful board book perfect for little ones ages two through five. Each open page features a fun Halloween scene with white shapes waiting to be filled with water. Simply brush water over the shapes and watch the colors magically appear! It’s an interactive way for young children to enjoy the excitement of Halloween.
Jasper Rabbit’s Creepy Tales! Unsettling Salad! , by Aaron Reynolds and brilliantly illustrated using digital drawing and pencil on paper by Peter Brown, is another great addition to this delightful, slightly chilling, fun, and funny series. When a badger and an opossum eat an entire salad, something creepy happens with the salad—and things quickly become unsettling. The atmospheric illustrations appear on almost every page and perfectly complement the story. This early chapter book is a great choice for ages six through nine.
Monsters Play…Trick or Treat! (The World of Gustavo), by Flavia Z. Drago, is a brightly illustrated board book made especially for babies and toddlers. With lift-the-flaps on every open page, little ones can join Shelley the bat as she discovers whether each surprise is a trick or a treat. The colorful illustrations and interactive flaps make this a fun Halloween read for the youngest trick-or-treaters.
Beware the Werewolf: The Graphic Novel (Desmond Cole Ghost Patrol) is a continuation of this popular middle-grade reader series, this time in a graphic novel format. The town is dealing with a frightfully awful dog catcher who is gathering up all the dogs he can find. The bright, colorful illustrations help bring the spooky adventure to life. This fun and engaging read will keep kids ages five through nine turning the pages.
Spooky Pookie, by Sandra Boynton, is a silly and adorable board book for babies and toddlers. This rhyming tale follows Pookie, a cute little pig, as he tries to figure out which costume to choose for Halloween. Young readers will have fun following along as Pookie considers his options, and his final choice is sure to delight everyone who reads it.
Please Don’t Scare the Ghost , by Carrie Williford and colorfully illustrated by Allysa Adams, is a fun and cute picture book with a clever premise. Readers learn how to take care of their friendly ghost on Halloween and, more importantly, how to keep the ghost from becoming scared. A witch, Frankenstein, and a mummy are just a few of the creatures children encounter along the way. A fun choice for ages three to eight.
Clifford’s Halloween , by Norman Bridwell, has sturdy pages that are perfect for little hands. Children ages two through six can celebrate Halloween with Clifford the Big Red Dog and his BFF, Emily, as they enjoy their favorite holiday of the year. Clifford’s familiar charm makes this a comforting Halloween choice for young fans, while the shiny foil cover makes the book extra special.
Spooky Scouts , by Kimberly Shrack, is an adorable story about a camping trip where Luna has to keep a secret. As the full moon begins to appear, Luna wonders—and worries—about what she will turn into. This sweet story combines friendship, bravery, and just the right amount of spooky spirit. The colorful digital illustrations add to the fun and make this a delightful Halloween read.
The Haunted Goldfish: Ready-to-Read Level 3 (Night Frights) , by Joe McGee and brightly illustrated by Teo Skaffa, is a perfect choice for new readers ages six through eight. Victor is saying goodbye to his goldfish, Doris, who has passed away, and he flushes her down the toilet. But Doris has other plans! This silly and entertaining story is sure to get young readers laughing while giving them a fun Halloween-themed book they can read on their own.
The House With Nobody In It , by Jon Klassen, is a clever board book for ages three to seven, filled with die-cut surprises peeking through the pages. The book itself is shaped like a house, but as readers move from page to page, they discover that something is missing. With Klassen’s distinctive artwork and clever design, this is a little book that offers plenty to discover. This one is a treasure!
summary: House of Harness (A Scarlet Witch Graphic Novel), by Preeti Chhibber and colorfully illustrated by Jodi Nishijima and Kiichi Mizushima, follows teen Wanda Eger as she begins at a magical school. Halloween (Water Wonders), published by Kane Miller and cleverly and brightly illustrated by Laura Garrido Amador, is a colorful board book perfect for little ones ages two through five. Unsettling Salad!, by Aaron Reynolds and brilliantly illustrated using digital drawing and pencil on paper by Peter Brown, is another great addition to this delightful, slightly chilling, fun, and funny series.
